rationale: Validation status is fail and mutation_score (0.875) exceeds the 0.5 floor, but the uncovered_requirement issue for SR4 disqualifies auto-retain since validation_status=fail. Examining mutant_SR4_domain_specific_001: it genuinely corrupts the rationale so it no longer references scan_en/scan-mode conditionality (capture/shift), and instead mischaracterizes the leak as a constant always-on wiring defect unrelated to any control signal -- this is a real, observable corruption of the exact property SR4 is meant to check (scan-mode-conditional understanding vs generic/always-on bug framing). Yet mutation_baseline_run and the mutation report show 0/1 targeting mutants detected for SR4, meaning evaluate.py's SR4 check (keyword/semantic presence check for terms like scan_en/capture/shift) still passed this mutant even though the analyzer's own evidence describes the SR4 check as keyword-based and 'insufficiently robust against near-miss submissions.' This is a genuine detection gap in the evaluator, not a defective mutant, so evaluation_framework must be revised.
revision_instructions: Strengthen the SR4 check in evaluate.py so it actually fails when a rationale describes the leak as a permanent/always-on/constant wiring or connectivity defect independent of any control signal, rather than as conditional on scan-mode (scan_en-gated capture/shift). Concretely: (1) require the rationale to explicitly assert that the exposure depends on scan_en being asserted (i.e. the mechanism is off/absent when scan_en=0), not merely contain the substring 'scan_en' or 'capture' or 'shift' in isolation -- a rationale can mention these words while simultaneously claiming the leak is constant/always-present, and the check must catch that contradiction; (2) add a negative pattern check that fails the rationale if it characterizes the defect using language like 'permanent', 'always', 'regardless of any control signal', 'stuck', 'unrelated to any test-mode signal', or similarly asserts the leak is present in every cycle/mode rather than gated by scan_en; (3) optionally use the available iverilog/vvp cross-check by toggling scan_en=0 vs scan_en=1 against the netlist and comparing to the submission's claimed always-on behavior, failing SR4 if the submission's description is inconsistent with the observed scan_en-gated behavior of the netlist. After the fix, re-run mutation testing and confirm the mutant that reframes the leak as a constant/always-on wiring bug (targeting SR4) is now detected.
